text:
jess: hey — running into flaky http2 RST_STREAM errors from the Go client when cancelling contexts mid-stream. Happens on long streaming responses from the server. Anyone seen this pattern?

aaron: yup, seen it before. usually when the client cancels but the transport tries to reuse the connection for another stream. http2 multiplexing means canceling a stream doesn't always close the TCP conn, so server-side resets can bubble back.

maria: do you have a minimal repro? curious if it's specifically Request.WithContext vs canceling a goroutine that's reading from resp.Body.

jess: reproducible with a simple client: send request with ctx that we cancel after 2s while reading resp.Body. code:```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 30 * time.Second,
}
http2.ConfigureTransport(tr)
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
resp, err := client.Do(req)
// read stream in a loop, then ctx cancel -> sometimes RST_STREAM in logs
```

tim: a few things to try: 1) explicitly call resp.Body.Close() when cancelling (best-effort) so the stream is released; 2) for endpoints where we expect frequent cancels, consider DisableKeepAlives to avoid reusing connections for other requests; 3) tune IdleConnTimeout / MaxIdleConnsPerHost so idle streams don't pile up.

olivia: +1 on resp.Body.Close(). One trick: wrap the read loop and listen on ctx.Done() to call resp.Body.Close() from another goroutine on cancel.

aaron: also check whether you configure http2 via net/http automatic upgrade or via golang.org/x/net/http2 ConfigureTransport — different behaviors observed in older Go versions. which go version is this?

jess: using go1.20.4 in CI. server is nginx-based ingress with http2 proxying.

maria: nginx + http2 + upstreams can also inject RST_STREAM if it thinks stream is stale. worth testing direct to server (bypass ingress) to rule that out.

tim: for transport tuning, here are some practical settings we've used in SDK:```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns: 200,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 100,
  IdleConnTimeout: 15 * time.Second,
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 5 * time.Second,
  // optionally disable keepalives for critical streaming endpoints
  // DisableKeepAlives: true,
}
http2.ConfigureTransport(tr)
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr, Timeout: 0} // Timeout handled by ctx
```

olivia: fwiw we added a small wrapper in the SDK: when streaming, set a header to indicate "no-reuse" and on client we set DisableKeepAlives for those requests only. not ideal perf-wise but avoids weird cross-stream resets during aggressive cancellations.

aaron: one more subtlety: context propagation into goroutines reading the stream. if you spawn a goroutine to process resp.Body you must pass the ctx into that goroutine and ensure it listens for Done and closes resp.Body. otherwise cancellation in one goroutine may not propagate properly.

jess: great tips. i'll try the resp.Body.Close on cancel + transport tuning + direct-to-server test. i'll report back with a tiny repro repo. thanks all :thumbsup:
